title: Amide-bond replacements and measured biological activity
claim: Monofluoroalkenes have been investigated as selected peptide amide-bond replacements.
source_passage: Monofluoroalkenes are fluorinated motifs that can be used to replace amide bonds.
source_location: Author abstract; publisher full text Introduction and applications.
transfer_limit: Not a statement that the project products are drugs, or that every amide replacement improves activity.
interpretation: Selected monofluoroalkenes have been investigated as peptide amide-bond replacements. In the cited example, fluorinated analogues showed weak to moderate anti-HIV activity but lower potency than SC29EK. This supports an explored medicinal application; it does not establish improved activity or drug status for the present products.

title: Proposed mimics of amide derivatives and phosphates

title: Selectivity across fluorinated alkene reaction partners
claim: Selective defluorinative construction of functionalized monofluoroalkenes faces regio-, stereo- and pathway-selectivity demands.
source_passage: the initial hydronickelation step must proceed with significantly different reactivities due to the presence of C = C double bonds in the alkene, the gem-difluoroalkene, and the monofluoroalkene product.
source_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning Recently; primary abstract and Results for successful coupling.
transfer_limit: NiH coupling of preformed gem-difluoroalkenes, not the project’s saturated CF3 carbonyl/Nu donor conditions.
interpretation: The cited NiH study highlights the need to distinguish the reactivities of an alkene, a gem-difluoroalkene and a monofluoroalkene product during hydronickelation. It provides context for regio-, stereo- and pathway-selectivity questions. Its preformed gem-difluoroalkene coupling partners differ from the saturated CF₃ carbonyl substrates and donor conditions examined here.

transfer_limit: Cu/borylation of polyfluoroalkenes, not exact project RCOCH2CF3/heteroatom transformation. The described atorvastatin mimic does not establish broad medicinal deployment.
